questions.text: A healthcare organization is participating in a Medicare Shared Savings Program (MSSP) contract at the BASIC Track. The organization performs well on quality measures but exceeds the benchmark cost target for the year. What is the financial consequence?

options.a: The organization receives a partial shared savings payment proportional to quality scores
options.b: The organization must repay a portion of excess costs to CMS
options.c: The organization receives no shared savings but faces no financial penalty
options.d: The organization is automatically moved to the ENHANCED Track with downside risk

questions.explanation: The organization receives no shared savings but faces no financial penalty The MSSP BASIC Track is an upside-only model. Organizations share in savings if costs come in below benchmark but face no penalty if they exceed the benchmark. This is the defining feature of upside-only risk — reward without downside exposure.

questions.text: Social determinants of health (SDOH) are estimated to drive approximately what percentage of health outcomes?
questions.explanation: 80% SDOH drive approximately 80% of health outcomes — far exceeding the contribution of clinical care. This figure is a high-yield exam fact. The key insight is that patients cannot be effectively treated to target if upstream determinants (housing, food, transport, income) are ignored.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the key difference between upside-only and two-sided risk models in Alternative Payment Models?

options.a: Upside-only models include quality bonuses; two-sided models do not
options.b: Two-sided models require higher data and care coordination capacity than upside-only models
options.c: Upside-only models apply only to physician groups; two-sided models apply only to hospitals
options.d: Two-sided models eliminate the need for quality measurement entirely

questions.explanation: Two-sided models require higher data and care coordination capacity than upside-only models Risk progression demands stronger data, analytics, and care coordination at each step. Two-sided risk requires organizations to have mature data infrastructure and care management systems to manage the financial exposure.

questions.text: The HCP-LAN framework categorizes payment models on a spectrum. Which category represents the most advanced tier of value-based payment?
questions.explanation: Category 4: Population-Based Payment HCP-LAN Category 4 (population-based payment, e.g., global capitation) is the most advanced APM tier. It represents the complete shift away from volume-based payment toward full population accountability.

questions.text: The Maryland Total Cost of Care Model differs from most Medicare payment models because:

options.a: It applies only to physician practices, not hospitals
options.b: It uses a tiered payment system based on quality scores
options.c: All payers — not just Medicare — participate under global hospital budgets
options.d: It penalizes hospitals only when readmission rates exceed national averages

questions.explanation: All payers — not just Medicare — participate under global hospital budgets The Maryland model is an All-Payer Model in which all payers participate in a global hospital budget structure. Hospitals receive a fixed annual budget regardless of volume, reversing the traditional incentive to maximize admissions.
